neighbours.label: The word after 'holds', 'serves' or 'appointed' where a position, record or membership follows (holds the title, serves on the board, appointed to the panel); similar verbs stay low
fire: Mr. Vance holds the title of senior partner at the firm.
Since last year she serves on the parish council.
Dr. Ito was appointed to the review panel in March.
Ms. Reyes currently holds the post of treasurer.
He serves on the board of two local charities.
She was appointed to the bench by the governor.
Our coach holds the national record in the mile.
The senator serves in the armed services committee.
quiet: Mr. Vance carries the bags of the senior partner at the firm.
Since last year she brings cakes to the parish hall.
Dr. Ito was invited to the review dinner in March.
Ms. Reyes currently likes the taste of mango.
He sits on the bench of two local parks.
She was driven to the station by the governor.
Our coach broke the wooden chair in the mess.
The senator serves soup at the armed forces shelter.

short: holds the, serves on, appointed to
notes: Second round. Round 1 ('occupying an office') failed because 'holds the ladder' (0.49) and 'serves soup' (0.32) fired. The label is lowered to the words: 'holds the' fires for any object, so one such near miss is not expected to separate and fire items use position-like objects. A probe of 'She serves tea' read 0.15.
